metadata.title: School Accountability, Autonomy, Choice, and the Equity of Student Achievement (EN)

survey_design.weight_fields_interpretation: The report uses PISA 2003’s two-stage sampling design (schools as PSUs, then students within schools) and estimates cross-country education production functions at the student level. It applies weighted least squares using students’ sampling probabilities to obtain coefficient estimates consistent with a census of the student population within each country, and it normalizes sampling weights so that countries contribute equally to the international estimates. Standard errors are adjusted for the hierarchical survey structure by using clustering-robust linear regression with clustering at the school level (and country-level clustering for non-interacted country-level variables). The manuscript does not report replicate-weight methods (e.g., BRR/jackknife), so replicate-weight variance estimation is not used or not documented here.

data.handling_not_reported_explanation: Plausible values are not applicable because the dependent variables are PISA test scores used in an econometric production-function framework rather than PV-based achievement modeling as in typical ILSA PV workflows. Missing data handling is implemented via conditional mean imputation with model-based predictions and the inclusion of imputation dummies and interactions to mitigate bias from non-random missingness; the report does not describe Rubin-style PV pooling because PVs are not the analysis target here.

sample_details.sample_filtering_criteria: The analytic dataset is constructed from PISA 2003 for 15-year-old students in OECD countries, yielding 181,469 students across 27 OECD countries. France is excluded because PISA 2003 lacks school-level background information for sampled schools; Mexico and Turkey are excluded because their average ESCS is one standard deviation below the international mean, which the authors argue could distort equity comparisons. Students with missing ESCS are dropped, while missing values in other background variables are imputed using conditional mean imputation; the models include imputation dummies and interactions to control for observations with imputed values. The report focuses primarily on mathematics achievement (and also estimates science as a reference), using country-level averages of institutional features to avoid within-country self-selection.

data.outcome_summary: This OECD report analyzes how national school accountability, autonomy, and choice relate to the equity of student achievement across countries, using PISA 2003 microdata. The target equity concept is operationalized as how strongly student mathematics achievement depends on family socio-economic status (SES), measured by PISA’s ESCS index; the key estimands are interaction effects between country-level institutional features and student-level ESCS. The study constructs a student-level micro database (181,469 students in 27 OECD countries) and excludes France, Mexico, and Turkey for data comparability reasons, while dropping students with missing ESCS. Missing background questionnaire data are handled via conditional mean imputation with imputation dummies and interactions, and estimation uses weighted least squares with PISA sampling probabilities plus clustering-robust standard errors to respect the hierarchical survey design. Because institutional variables are measured at the country level, the analysis emphasizes between-country variation and avoids within-country self-selection, but it limits degrees of freedom and precludes detailed interactions among institutional features.
data.null_fields_interpretation: This is an OECD technical report using micro-econometric regression models rather than machine-learning predictive modeling, so fields related to ML algorithms and predictive performance are intentionally empty. The report also does not present PV-based ML targets; instead it models achievement and equity via interactions with ESCS and country-level institutional measures. As a result, the extraction contains no StructuredFinding rows and no conceptual confounder list in the ML schema, even though the report includes many questionnaire and school controls.
